newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN ITALY'S SERIE A.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN ITALY'S SERIE A.

text.p: Italian Serie A matches due to be played on Sunday (league placings in parentheses, kick-off times GMT):

Only the suspension of Bologna's Swedish striker Kennet Andersson offers much hope to Atalanta, beaten by Lazio, AC Milan and Udinese in their last three outings. Davide Fontolan replaces Andersson alongside Russian Igor Kolyvanov and Carlo Nervo in the Bologna attack, while Atalanta as usual look to Gigi Lentini, Domenico Morfeo and Filippo Inzaghi, the latter still leading the list of Serie A marksmen on 18.

Following that historic 6-1 drubbing by Juventus last week, Milan would have probably wished for any rival other than Inter next time out. Milan will be the better for the return of Alessandro Costacurta in defence and Liberian George Weah alongside Marco Simone in attack. Inter are on a wave, following their 3-1 UEFA Cup, semifinal first leg win against French side Monaco on Tuesday and should field a full-strength side with French schemer Youri Djorkaeff again playing behind strikers Maurizio Ganz and Ivan Zamorano.

What price Udinese after wins for Juventus over AC Milan (6-1 in the league) and Dutch side Ajax Amsterdam (2-1 in a European Cup semifinal first leg in Amsterdam on Wednesday)? Udinese can take faint hope from the growing list of injured at Juventus, with strikers Alen Boksic and Alessandro Del Piero both still out and with another striker, Christian Vieri, doubtful. Attilio Lombardo is on standby to partner Nicola Amoruso in the Juventus attack while German Oliver Bierhoff and Paolo Poggi lead the Udinese front line.

With eight games to play it is do-or-die time for relegation battlers Cagliari, encouraged by a 2-1 win against AS Roma last week. Meanwhile, Napoli have spent the week calling foul following Perugia's suspect equaliser in a 1-1 draw last Sunday. In short, both sides are motivated. Brazilian Andre Cruz and Fabio Pecchia could be the key figures for Napoli, while Cagliari again look to the experience of striker Sandro Tovalieri.

An upset could be on the cards here if Fiorentina are either tired or in a state of anti-climax following their 1-1 away draw with Barcelona in a Cup Winners' Cup semifinal first leg on Thursday night. Relegation battlers Piacenza need the points and look to Andrea Tentoni and Gian Pietro Piovani in attack. Fiorentina welcome back Russian winger Andrei Kanchelskis and Swedish midfielder Stefan Schwarz, both missing on Thursday.

Out of form Vicenza, held to a 0-0 draw by Verona last week, could pick up useful points against a Reggiana side all but mathematically relegated. Giovanni Cornacchini partners Uruguayan Marcelo Otero in the Vicenza attack while Reggiana look to Colombian Adolfo Valencia and Russian Igor Simutenkov.

The 74-year-old Swedish maestro Nils Liedholm returns to the fray on the Roma bench following the midweek departure of Argentine coach Carlos Bianchi. His first game back is a tough one against in-form Parma. Liedholm is likely to play a cautious 4-4-2 with Argentine Abel Balbo and Francesco Totti leading the attack. Parma will be without striker Enrico Chiesa and Croatian midfielder Mario Stanic, both injured. In their absence, Argentine Hernan Crespo leads the attack alongside Alessandro Melli.

Sampdoria's Swedish coach Sven Eriksson comes face to face with his future since he will be coach to Lazio next season. Sampdoria are without injured Serb libero Sinisa Mihajlovic but field Vincenzo Montella and captain Roberto Mancini in attack, while Lazio are without injured strikers Pierluigi Casiraghi and Igor Protti. Lazio captain Giuseppe Signori may go it alone up front in a game vital to the UEFA Cup qualifying prospects of both clubs.

Perugia may pick up vital points in this relegation battle against Verona, another side which already seems all but mathematically relegated. Croatian striker Milan Rapajic, scorer of a disputed "Hand of God" style goal against Napoli last week, is out through suspension leaving Marco Negri and Fausto Pizzi to lead the attack. Verona look to Filippo Maniero and Nicola Zanini up front.
